concept_summary: The fantasy of Account-free daily microgames with a deliberate no-monetization stance stretched over a single persistent season lasting months: one meaningful decision per evening, no grinding, no catching up. Progress compounds across real calendar time and a missed week bends the story instead of ending it. The finale is scheduled, shared, and unrepeatable.
first_experiment: Concierge test: run the core decision by hand over seven daily messages with three players; if day-seven return beats the source's second-session return, the long form has legs.
source_idea_title: Account-free daily microgames with a deliberate no-monetization stance
why_it_is_opposite: While the source fits daily, this concept flips the clock: one season here outlasts hundreds of source sessions, so the source habit of quick payoff actively hurts.

concept_summary: A reverse-loop game in the world of Tiny planet you can circumnavigate in minutes: you begin holding everything the source hands out and win by giving it all back. Where the source loop is 'A bounded curved world with no map screen: progress is spatial and memorable because the whole world fits in the player's head.', here every move undoes the 'A bounded curved world with no map screen: progress is spatial and memorable because the whole world fits in the player's head.' loop step by step instead of advancing it, so the map empties and the score falls. Hoarding triggers the lose state; the end screen celebrates an empty board.
first_experiment: Paper prototype: ten tokens stand in for everything the player owns and each turn must discard at least one; test with five players whether emptying the board feels like winning after three rounds.
source_idea_title: Tiny planet you can circumnavigate in minutes
why_it_is_opposite: While the source rewards accumulation (A bounded curved world with no map screen: progress is spatial and memorable because the whole world fits in the player's head.), this concept rewards the opposite: progress means having less, so a winning run here would score zero in the source.

concept_summary: The fantasy of Single-file 3D kart racer on WebGPU replanted on one shared map where every player acts at once and every move is visible. Resources, storms, and scarcities hit everyone simultaneously, so private optimization loses to public negotiation. The game only functions above fifty concurrent players.
first_experiment: Moderated crowd test: put fifteen volunteers on one shared board for twenty minutes; if alliances form without prompting, the social layer carries the game.
why_it_is_opposite: While the source is a private experience, this concept flips it into a crowd: playing alone is impossible here, whereas the source never requires another person.
